name: ICARUS
full_name: Imaging Cosmic And Rare Underground Signals
summary: ICARUS pioneered large liquid-argon TPC operation at Gran Sasso and now serves as the far detector of Fermilab's Short-Baseline Neutrino programme. The Italian and US deployments are phases of the same T600 detector.
physics_targets: Short-baseline neutrino oscillations and sterile-neutrino tests
detection_principle: Ionization charge drifts through purified liquid argon to wire planes, creating detailed three-dimensional tracks and electromagnetic showers. Scintillation light supplies event timing; external cosmic-ray tagging is essential for the shallow Fermilab deployment.

key_parameters.name: Additional beam
key_parameters.value: Also receives an off-axis NuMI neutrino flux

results.summary: The first BNB oscillation analysis, using 2022-2023 data, found no statistically significant muon-neutrino disappearance and reported 90% confidence exclusion contours within its stated two-neutrino approximation of a 3+1 model. Flux and interaction uncertainties limit the single-detector result.
Published the first Fermilab ICARUS neutrino cross-section measurement using off-axis NuMI data, with differential quasielastic-like interaction distributions on argon.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
